claims.text: Fine-tuning the Si:Ge ratio of Gd5(Si,Ge)4 will improve its magnetocaloric performance near room temperature.
Adding small amounts of selected transition metals to Gd5(Si,Ge)4 will improve its magnetocaloric performance near room temperature.
Compositional modification enhances magnetostructural coupling in Gd5(Si,Ge)4.
The enhanced magnetostructural coupling arises from changes in the crystal lattice caused by compositional modification.
The enhanced magnetostructural coupling arises from changes in electronic interactions caused by compositional modification.
Selective substitution modifies an order-disorder phase transition in Gd5(Si,Ge)4.
Selective substitution tunes the lattice parameters of Gd5(Si,Ge)4.
Selective substitution tunes the electronic structure of Gd5(Si,Ge)4.
Tuning the phase transition, lattice parameters, and electronic structure reduces thermal hysteresis.
Tuning the phase transition, lattice parameters, and electronic structure increases the isothermal entropy change under moderate magnetic fields.
Tuning the phase transition, lattice parameters, and electronic structure increases the adiabatic temperature change under moderate magnetic fields.
Modified Gd5(Si,Ge)4 will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric effect than the unmodified alloy near room temperature.
Standard Gd5(Si,Ge)4 requires relatively high magnetic fields for effective magnetocaloric operation.
Standard Gd5(Si,Ge)4 exhibits significant thermal hysteresis.
Departures from optimal substitution levels may eliminate the proposed magnetocaloric benefits.
Operation outside near-ambient temperatures or moderate magnetic-field cycles may eliminate the proposed benefits.
